If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast slope in mid-horizon (days 10–20) by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast slope in early horizon (days 1–7) by 5–10% to compensate for downward bias.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast peak to later horizon (days 15–25) and reduce peak magnitude by 10–15%.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across 5+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path, reducing volatility in late horizon (days 20–30) by 10–15%.

If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (≥0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), increase forecast tail in late horizon (days 25–30) by 5–10% to capture momentum carryover.

If sentiment shows strong downward momentum (≤-0.33 for 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast tail in late horizon (days 25–30) by 5–10% and add early correction at day 15–20 to prevent overshoot.
